Hi Emma — thanks, and appreciated the questions. Putting concise answers below and flagging a couple of configuration options. I copied our Security lead (Vivek) and Solutions (Laura/Marissa) for detail and next steps.

Short answers for InfoSec (one-paragraph each):
- Prompt text & outputs: By default, Redwood logs request metadata and short-lived session artifacts to support routing and billing. Customer prompt text and full assistant outputs are NOT persisted in long-term storage by default for Hosted accounts; they are held in an ephemeral cache that may exist for up to 24 hours for routing/KV-cache warmup, then pruned unless customer enables storage. If you opt into "retained logs" for debugging or analytics, those are stored separately with explicit customer consent.
- Token-level logs: We capture aggregated token-level metrics for billing and performance; raw token streams are not stored unless retention is enabled.
- Residency: For Hosted mode customers, persisted artifacts (if retention is enabled) are written to the region you select during onboarding. HealthScope appears to be in us-west-2 by default; ephemeral caches may be routed through regional gateways but do not leave US regions unless cross-region routing is requested.
- TTLs: Ephemeral cache default TTL is 24 hours; retained logs default TTL is 90 days. We can support custom TTLs as low as 7 days for retained logs and 0 days (no persistence) for strict PII workflows.

Config knobs: data-retention-policy (per-workspace), per-route retention overrides, and a prompt-data classifier that can tag prompt sessions as "PII" to enforce stricter retention and disable retention automatically.

Next steps I propose: 1) Vivek to share SOC2 and a sample DPA paragraph on retention; 2) Laura to propose minimal config values (region confirmation, TTL) for HealthScope to sign off; 3) We prepare a one-page summary Emma can attach to the ticket.

I'll follow up with the artifacts shortly.

Emma — quick security note and attached artifacts.

What we are sharing: SOC 2 Type II summary (redacted), our standard DPA clause for retention & processing, and a short Ops checklist describing how to opt into zero-retention mode. Key points below you can extract for InfoSec:
- Encryption: All persisted artifacts are encrypted at rest with customer-managed KMS where requested; in Hosted default we use Redwood-managed KMS.
- Access controls: Retained logs are accessible only to a small set of production SRE/service accounts; access is audited and logged in our audit trail.
- Auditability: Audit logs (who accessed retained data and when) are retained for 365 days and can be exported on request.
- Data residency guarantee: When retention is enabled, data is written only to the region you choose (we will provision buckets and encryption keys in that region). Ephemeral caching may transiently touch neighboring regional services for performance but will not write to long-term storage outside the chosen residency.

If HealthScope requires on-prem/private deployment, we can provide the Private deployment package and walk through the air-gapped architecture.

Attaching: SOC2_Report_2028.pdf, dpa-draft-healthscope.docx

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni

1) Can you confirm the exact TTL options are configurable per workspace or per-route? We need per-route control so anything with PHI can be zero-retention while other routes keep 90d for analytics.
2) For ephemeral cache: does it ever get written to S3 buckets in us-west-2 during the 24-hour window, or is it purely in-memory/local SSD and pruned? InfoSec is okay with transient SSDs but wants assurance it's not synced to long-term object storage.
3) If we opt into customer-managed KMS, will Redwood need key access for any emergency debugging? What's the process for emergency key use and how will it be audited?

If you can respond to these three items in one short paragraph each, we can attach and move to procurement — thanks.

— Emma
